title: DARPA AIxCC Autonomous Cyber Reasoning Systems Find and Patch 18 Real Zero-Day Bugs Across 54M LOC
aiSystem: Team Atlanta & DARPA AIxCC Cyber Reasoning Systems
whyItMatters: At DARPA AIxCC Finals (DEF CON 33), autonomous AI systems audited 54M lines of C/Java open-source code, discovering and patching 43/54 synthetic bugs plus 18 real zero-days (11 patched) at ~$152 per task.
summary: In the Final Competition of DARPA and ARPA-H’s two-year AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC) at DEF CON 33—systematically analyzed in USENIX Security 2026 (arXiv:2602.07666)—seven autonomous LLM-and-fuzzer Cyber Reasoning Systems (won by Team Atlanta from Georgia Tech, Samsung Research, KAIST, and POSTECH, followed by Trail of Bits and Theori) audited 54 million lines of real-world C and Java open-source software without human intervention. Finalist systems found 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities (86%) and patched 43 (68%), while also uncovering 18 previously unknown real-world zero-day vulnerabilities (6 in C, 12 in Java) and autonomously generating 11 real patches in an average of 45 minutes at ~$152 per task.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously analyzed 54 million lines of production open-source C and Java code, discovering 86% (54/63) and patching 68% (43/63) of challenge vulnerabilities.
Uncovered 18 genuine, non-synthetic zero-day vulnerabilities in real open-source projects and generated 11 working patches autonomously.
Average turnaround of 45 minutes per patch at ~$152 per task, with all seven finalist Cyber Reasoning Systems open-sourced for critical-infrastructure defense.
caveats: Evaluated inside a structured DARPA competition harness; real-world deployment on arbitrary enterprise codebases still requires integration with build systems, regression suites, and maintainer review.

scoreRationale.foundational: Marks the inflection point where fully autonomous neuro-symbolic AI systems both discover and patch real zero-day bugs at multi-million-LOC scale.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly transforms global open-source and critical-infrastructure cybersecurity with seven open-sourced Cyber Reasoning Systems.
scoreRationale.verification: Independently scored live by DARPA/ARPA-H at DEF CON 33 and peer-reviewed in USENIX Security 2026 (SoK paper).
scoreRationale.velocity: Compresses weeks of human security auditing and patch engineering into ~45 minutes and ~$152 per task.
